title: AUTHORED TEST: REPRESENT-D2 two-step area-preserving grid translations
subject: TEST
scope_summary: Wholly original unit-grid representation task: map a fully specified colored grid into disjoint rectangles, then a row-count/product representation while preserving the set of cells. Changed transfer reverses numerical row-length representation into a notch geometry. No official Q002 question or diagram used.

supports_claims: Primary five rows seven columns, left two columns shaded plus top two rows of remaining five shaded, leave 15 square units.
Six row lengths 8,8,5,5,5,5 reconstruct a 6×8 full rectangle minus lower-right 3×4 notch, leaving 36 squares.

conventions.statement: Every drawn grid cell is a 1-by-1 square with unit area; a rows-by-columns rectangle has the product number of cells.
Regions in a subtraction decomposition must have no overlapping counted cells.
A left-aligned row-length list states which cells belong to each row, but does not itself hand over a surrounding-rectangle decomposition.

capabilities.action: REPRESENT the same visible unit cells using a nonoverlapping rectangular partition and a row-count/product view, with a check that total cell count is invariant.
capabilities.success_criterion: For a 5×7 grid shaded in a left strip of width 2 and a top right band of height 2, map to both 35−10−10 and three rows of five, giving 15; transfer reconstruct from row lengths 8,8,5,5,5,5 into 6×8 minus 3×4.

microtopics.title: Preserve cell count through grid, disjoint rectangle and row-length mappings
microtopics.badge_reason: Coordinate two representation choices and a nonoverlap check; arithmetic itself is routine.
entry_assumptions: Read rows and columns of an equal-unit grid.
Use rectangle area as row count times column count.
Distinguish cells being removed from cells remaining.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Convert visually overlapping shade descriptions into a pair of DISJOINT removed rectangles, then independently represent the SAME remaining cells with row counts or a rectangular product.

teaching_path.action: Read a 6-by-6 grid of unit squares and locate the top two rows.
teaching_path.why_valid: An equal-unit grid has 6×6=36 squares; the top two rows cover 2×6.

teaching_path.action: After marking the complete top two rows, mark the right two columns ONLY in the four remaining rows.
teaching_path.why_valid: Disjoint-region accounting prevents counting any top-right square in two removed areas.

teaching_path.action: Match unmarked squares to a bottom-left 4-by-4 rectangle.
teaching_path.why_valid: The unaffected rows/columns meet to form exactly 4×4 surviving equal cells.

teaching_path.action: Count in two independent representations: difference 36−12−8 and 4-by-4 product.
teaching_path.why_valid: Every cell belongs to exactly one of top band, lower-right band and the remaining region.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Subtract the full area of the top two rows and then also the full area of the right two columns of a 6×6 grid, counting four corner cells twice.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Point to the four top-right cells. Are they removed once or included in both parts of your subtraction?
misconceptions.repair: After removing two entire top rows, the right strip has height four, not six. Check 36−12−8=16 against the remaining 4×4 grid.

exit_task.prompt: Independently: a 4-row, 7-column unit grid has its entire leftmost column shaded and the bottom row of the remaining 6 columns shaded. Translate into TWO cell-count representations: a non-overlapping subtraction from the full grid and a product for the remaining unshaded rectangle. Give the common number of unshaded cells and justify that no shaded cell was removed twice.

answer.summary: Eighteen unshaded squares in both representations.
reasoning: Left strip has 1×4=4, and bottom-right band has 1×6=6; these are disjoint.
Remaining 28−4−6=18; it also forms 3 rows of 6 columns, or 3×6=18.
answer.check: Independent check: 4+6+18=28; each of the three groups uses distinct cells.

microtopics.research_contribution: Original D2 visual-to-symbolic grid translation, a separate false-overlap reconstruction and true reverse row-length transfer, all as TEST-only authored content.

construction_units.decision: Map whole-grid shading into non-overlapping subregions, then count the same remaining cells through a row profile or product.

compact_anchor.prompt: After covering the top two of six rows, how many rows are still available to the right-column shade?
compact_anchor.result: Only four bottom rows remain, preventing the top-right cells from being subtracted twice.

predict.prompt: A learner tries to shade the top two rows AND the rightmost two columns across the entire grid, then subtract both full areas. Which corner cells would the arithmetic mistakenly count twice?
predict.defensible_answer: The four top-right cells lie in both full strips, so a correct disjoint decomposition changes the right-strip height to four.

attempt.produces: A new independent two-representation square count, with explicit check that the subtracted regions are disjoint.

task.prompt: A 5-row ×8-column array of equal tiles has its ENTIRE top row shaded and its rightmost 3 columns shaded in the other four rows. With no solution yet provided, independently write a nonoverlap subtraction and a remaining-rectangle product that count the SAME unshaded cells. State the common count, then justify no double subtraction.
givens: Five rows, eight columns, unit square tiles.
Top row shaded across full width.
Rightmost three columns shaded in the other four rows.

route.ask: Which rows and columns belong to the first complete shaded strip?
route.why_this_ask: Locate a precise set of cells before counting.

route.ask: After that first strip, what cells remain eligible for the SECOND shaded strip?
route.why_this_ask: Eliminate overlap with cells already counted as removed.

route.ask: Can the untouched cells be represented as one rectangle or a row-length list?
route.why_this_ask: Require a second way of viewing the same invariant set.

route.ask: Do the disjoint parts and leftover cells add to the original full grid?
route.why_this_ask: Verify the correspondence is reversible and conserves cell counts.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Core1A stages 6×6 top/right marking and constructs a 4×4 remainder; Core1B starts from learner's invalid full-height subtraction and requires a new 5×8 independent two-view attempt.

boundary_test.prompt: Boundary with changed orientation: a 7-column ×4-row grid has its bottom TWO complete rows shaded, and the left TWO columns shaded only in the remaining TOP TWO rows. Give a disjoint subtraction, a product for remaining cells, and explain why subtracting the full-height left strip would duplicate cells. Attempt before disclosure.
boundary_test.answer: 28 cells total, bottom 2×7=14 shaded and upper-left 2×2=4 shaded; untouched top-right 2×5=10, confirmed 28−14−4=10. Subtracting 2×4 for the left strip instead would count the bottom-left 4 cells twice.
boundary_test.confirms: Even when both strip directions change, the intersection must be removed once; the untouched product matches disjoint subtraction.

relations.expression: For r×c equal unit cells, shade a full-height left strip of width a and a top strip of height b only across the c−a remaining columns: surviving cells = rc−ar−b(c−a)=(r−b)(c−a).
relations.meaning: Both a nonoverlap subtraction and a residual rectangle name exactly the same unshaded cells; the correspondence preserves unit area.

symbols.meaning: Shaded top band height in right remainder

conditions: Grid consists of equal unit squares.

questions.stem: In a 6×6 equal-unit square grid, shade the entire top 2 rows, and shade the rightmost 2 columns ONLY in the remaining 4 rows. Represent the unshaded count as (i) full grid minus disjoint bands and (ii) a remaining rectangle.
conditions: 6 rows by 6 columns of equal unit squares.
Right two columns shaded only in lower four rows.
questions.failure_signal: Subtracts the right two columns over all six rows as well as the top two rows; loses the shared top-right corner twice.

answer.summary: Sixteen untouched squares, by both descriptions.
reasoning: Lower-right shading is 2×4=8, and it does not overlap the top region.
Untouched 36−12−8=16; the same remaining cells form a 4×4 rectangle=16.

questions.stem: The diagram shows a 5-ROW ×7-COLUMN grid of identical unit-square tiles. ALL cells in the leftmost 2 columns are shaded; among the 5 columns to their right, ONLY the topmost 2 rows are shaded. You must represent the same number of UNSHADED cells in TWO ways: (1) subtract a pair of nonoverlapping shaded rectangles from the whole grid, and (2) read the remaining row-lengths and show an equivalent rectangle product. Write both expressions, the common value, and explain why subtracting 2 full columns plus 2 FULL rows from 35 would double-count.
conditions: Five equal-height rows, seven equal-width columns.
Left two columns shaded in every row.
Top two rows shaded among only the five rightmost columns.
Each unit square may be counted once in the complement.
Authored TEST geometry, not an official question.
questions.failure_signal: Writes 35−2×5−2×7=11 and fails to notice 4 duplicated top-left cells, or presents one expression without correspondence.

reasoning: Shaded left strip covers 2×5=10 cells. The separate upper-right block has 5×2=10 cells; these blocks are disjoint.
Subtract the two disjoint shaded blocks: 35−10−10=15.
Read unshaded row lengths: top two rows contain zero unshaded cells; each of the remaining three rows has five, giving 0+0+5+5+5=15=3×5.
Subtracting the top TWO FULL rows (2×7) as well as the left strip (2×5) double-counts the 2×2 top-left corner, falsely giving 11.
answer.check: Independent enumerative check: classify each cell as left shade, upper-right shade or lower-right unshaded; counts 10+10+15=35.

reasoning_route.action: Interpret all 35 cells and the two stated shade rules as sets of grid coordinates.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The two rules locate shading by columns then by rows in the remaining columns.

reasoning_route.action: Partition the shaded cells into left 2×5 and upper-right 5×2, excluding any intersection.
reasoning_route.why_valid: A chosen decomposition must be disjoint to preserve the original set of grid tiles.

reasoning_route.action: Translate the same remaining cells into row lengths or lower-right rectangle.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Upper two rows have no unshaded tiles; bottom three rows have five each.

reasoning_route.action: Compare both expressions and reconcile the entire grid.
reasoning_route.why_valid: 35−10−10=15 and 3×5=15; all cells counted exactly once.

rubric.criterion: Correctly read the full 5×7 equal-unit grid and two shaded positions.
Choose TWO disjoint shaded blocks 2×5 and 5×2, not two overlapping full strips.
Transform remaining cells into 3×5 or [0,0,5,5,5] row lengths and verify count 15.
rubric.evidence_of: Preserves cell-count invariant under two-step representation.

After your own attempt, make the removed blocks disjoint by counting the second band only outside the first strip, then compare the surviving rows with a rectangle product.

questions.stem: There is NO drawing. A shape is built from unit squares, with all rows LEFT-ALIGNED. Reading from TOP to BOTTOM, its six row lengths are: 8, 8, 5, 5, 5, 5. Reconstruct a six-row grid description and represent its area in TWO genuinely different ways: first by grouping complete row bands, then as one surrounding rectangle with ONE rectangular corner cut out. Identify EXACTLY which rows and columns are missing; prove both expressions count the same squares. Explain why removing three columns from ALL six rows would be wrong.
conditions: Exactly six rows; row lengths top-to-bottom 8,8,5,5,5,5.
Each occupied cell is a 1×1 square and all rows begin at the same left edge.
Use a complete surrounding 6×8 rectangle for the second view.
No diagram provided: learner reconstructs its location and cutout.

hints.text: Which two of the six rows are longest? Begin with their stated lengths and avoid deciding the missing region before decoding each row.

questions.failure_signal: Treats missing 3 cells as absent in every row, or draws the notch in upper rather than lower rows.

answer.summary: 36 squares: 2×8+4×5=36 and 6×8−4×3=36; missing lower-right 3 columns in rows 3 through 6.
reasoning: Represent the top TWO rows as an 8-column by 2-row band: 2×8=16 cells.
Represent the lower FOUR rows as 5-column by 4-row band: 4×5=20 cells; row grouping total=36.
Enclose the left-aligned shape in 6×8=48 cells. Its absent cells are the rightmost 3 columns ONLY of the bottom four rows, a 4×3 cutout=12.
Hence complement count 48−12=36, equal to the row-band count.
Cutting three columns from all SIX rows removes cells that are actually present in the first two full rows; false 48−18=30.
answer.check: Independent row enumeration 8+8+5+5+5+5=36; complement 48−12=36 and top band 16 plus lower band 20.

reasoning_route.action: Interpret row-length data as six left-aligned rows with top two longer.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The list defines exact occupied cells by row.
reasoning_route.output: Two rows of 8, four rows of 5.

reasoning_route.action: Reconstruct an enclosing 6×8 grid and locate a lower-right missing 4×3 rectangle.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Short lower four rows omit three rightmost cells each; first two rows omit none.

reasoning_route.action: Translate row bands and enclosing rectangle-with-notch into expressions.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Disjoint occupied row bands and a subtractive bounding rectangle count identical cells.

reasoning_route.action: Compute both as 36 and explain why cutting all six rows is false.
reasoning_route.why_valid: No absent cells in the first two rows; full-height 3-column cut would discard legitimate squares.

rubric.criterion: Decode row profile into top two full-width rows and four short rows.
Locate missing lower-right 4×3 notch in 6×8 frame and not a 6×3 cut.

rubric.evidence_of: Conserves unit-cell count in changed representation.

transfer.statement: Unlike a supplied shaded picture (Core2A), transfer starts with NO drawing, only a six-entry row-length profile. Learner reconstructs geometry, then maps to row-band and enclosing-rectangle-minus-notch expressions.
transfer.invariant: Unit-cell cardinality unchanged by converting a row-length list into a geometric union or complement.

novelty.why_new: Primary is given grid shading and partitions removed vs surviving; Core1B boundary also starts with a stated grid. Transfer instead has only row-length data and must invent geometry and identify a lower-right missing 4×3 notch, then reconcile two expressions.
